MS.AAD.1.1v1 ("Legacy authentication SHALL be blocked") primarily reduces risk from credential-based techniques in MITRE ATT&CK, notably:

- T1078 — Valid Accounts: blocking legacy auth reduces the ability for attackers to sign in with stolen/compromised credentials via protocols that bypass modern protections (MFA, token-based auth).
- T1110 — Brute Force
  - T1110.001 — Password Guessing
  - T1110.002 — Password Spraying
  - T1110.003 — Credential Stuffing

Why: legacy/authentication protocols (e.g., basic auth) do not support modern authentication features (MFA, conditional access signals, risk-based authentication), so blocking them prevents attackers from using automated credential-guessing/stuffing and from authenticating with stolen passwords via those protocols.

Short answer
- Create a Conditional Access policy that requires a phishing‑resistant authentication strength for all users (with only emergency/break‑glass exclusions).  
- Ensure phishing‑resistant methods (FIDO2 security keys, Windows Hello for Business, and/or certificate‑based auth or other supported passwordless methods) are enabled and available to users.  
- Verify the Authentication Methods Migration is set to Migration Complete (so new methods and strengths are enforced).

Detailed remediation steps (portal + verification)

1) Enable phishing‑resistant authentication methods
- Azure portal > Entra ID (Azure AD) > Security > Authentication methods.
- Enable and configure passwordless / phishing‑resistant methods you plan to use, typically:
  - FIDO2 Security Keys (recommended)
  - Windows Hello for Business
  - Certificate-based auth (if used)
  - Microsoft Authenticator password
